relevance_note: Case report of an adult with a GFAP variant and Alexander disease, plus a literature table of earlier carriers: "Sanger sequencing of the entire exonic sequences revealed a heterozygous substitution of Glu to Lys at codon 332, p.E332K, of the GFAP gene".
method_note: Read the paper directly; built the JSON with a short Python script (values typed from my reading, not transcribed by script) and checked every span verbatim. In-scope people: proband II-2 (also the Table column headed 'The present patient'); his mother I-3 (Alexander disease diagnosed postmortem by pathology, not genetically tested: no variant row); and the earlier-reported patients in the unnumbered literature Table, whose patients are columns headed by reference numbers: column 1 headed '(7)' (one patient, labelled 'Table column 1'), column 2 headed '(6)' (three patients in one column). Column '(6)' gives the three patients' values as comma-separated lists in one cell (e.g. Sex 'M, F, M', Age at onset '56, 53, 28'), without per-patient labels; following D-31 (no positional reading of multi-value cells) I did not assign these values to individual people, labelled them 'unnamed person 1-3' (rule 6), and recorded only values printed once for the whole column (variant, Form AO, source reference). This applies to every clinical and MRI row of column '(6)', including rows where all three values are equal (e.g. 'No, No, No'), so all their checklist items are 'not reported'. The p.[R330G; E332K] cis allele (cDNA cell 'c.988C>G and c.994G>A') is recorded as one variant row per person, not split. Table cells reading 'No' were taken as explicit absence (a word, not a symbol); 'ND' is defined as 'not described' and treated as not reported. Functional evidence (Bachetti et al., ref 8) and the authors' 'pathogenic' statement name p.E332K, so they are recorded for both p.E332K carriers; the Alexander Disease Lab database 'likely pathogenic' label is a database classification, not the authors', and is not recorded. Variant type left 'not reported': the paper describes 'substitution of Glu to Lys' but never calls this variant missense (only GFAP variants in general). Inheritance not reported: mother's DNA was not available. 'Blood tests and cerebrospinal fluid analysis results were normal' is recorded as excluding abnormal blood test results and abnormal CSF analysis only, nothing more specific. Contradiction: the text describes 'garland-like hyperintensity signals along the lateral ventricular walls' while the Figure 3 legend describes 'A garland-like low-intensity signal' on T2-weighted imaging; the observed row uses the text wording. Mother I-3: Rosenthal fibers are a pathological finding; the checklist item 'cerebral white matter abnormality' was left not reported for her because no imaging is described.
